title: Grade 8 French — Mon, Jun 01
description: L'imparfait — Day 1 of 5: Concept and formation (the nous-stem rule)
subject: french

questions.question: We have learned passé composé (avoir + être). This week: L'IMPARFAIT. What kind of tense is it?
options: Another PAST tense — for ongoing, habitual or descriptive past actions
questions.explanation: L'imparfait is a past tense used for actions that were ongoing ('was doing'), habitual ('used to do'), or for descriptions in the past — different from the completed actions of the passé composé.

questions.question: How do you find the stem (radical) of the imparfait for almost every verb?
options: Take the 'nous' form of the PRESENT and drop -ons
questions.explanation: The golden rule: take the present 'nous' form, drop '-ons', and that is the imparfait stem. nous parlons → parl-, nous finissons → finiss-, nous faisons → fais-.

questions.question: What are the imparfait endings (je, tu, il, nous, vous, ils)?
Form the imparfait of PARLER for 'je' (nous parlons → parl-):
questions.explanation: Stem 'parl-' + 'ais' = 'je parlais' = I was speaking / I used to speak.

questions.question: Form the imparfait of FINIR for 'tu' (nous finissons → finiss-):
questions.explanation: Stem 'finiss-' + 'ais' = 'tu finissais'. Note the -iss- carries over from the present 'nous' form.

questions.question: Form the imparfait of FAIRE for 'il' (nous faisons → fais-):
questions.explanation: Stem 'fais-' + 'ait' = 'il faisait' = he was doing / used to do. FAIRE is irregular in the present but regular in the imparfait via the nous-stem rule.

questions.question: Form the imparfait of PRENDRE for 'nous' (nous prenons → pren-):
questions.explanation: Stem 'pren-' + 'ions' = 'nous prenions' = we were taking / used to take.

questions.question: What does 'je mangeais' mean?
options: I was eating / I used to eat
questions.explanation: 'Je mangeais' (imparfait) = I was eating / I used to eat — an ongoing or habitual past action.

questions.question: Why is it 'je mangeais' with an 'e' (manger → nous mangeons → mange-)?
options: The 'e' is kept after 'g' before a/o to keep the soft 'g' sound
All verbs add an extra e
questions.explanation: Verbs in -ger keep the 'e' before endings starting with a/o to keep the soft g: je mangeais, tu mangeais, il mangeait, ils mangeaient (but nous mangions, vous mangiez).

questions.question: Form the imparfait of HABITER for 'je' (nous habitons → habit-):
questions.explanation: Stem 'habit-' + 'ais' = 'j'habitais' = I was living / I used to live.

questions.question: Form the imparfait of VOIR for 'ils' (nous voyons → voy-):
questions.explanation: Stem 'voy-' + 'aient' = 'ils voyaient' = they were seeing / used to see.

questions.question: Which is the correct imparfait stem for ÉCRIRE (nous écrivons)?
questions.explanation: Drop -ons from 'nous écrivons' → 'écriv-'. So j'écrivais, tu écrivais...

questions.question: Form the imparfait of BOIRE for 'vous' (nous buvons → buv-):
questions.explanation: Stem 'buv-' + 'iez' = 'vous buviez' = you were drinking / used to drink.

questions.question: Which ending goes with 'ils/elles' in the imparfait?
questions.explanation: Ils/elles → -aient (silent, pronounced like -ait): ils parlaient, elles finissaient.

questions.question: Complete: 'Quand j'étais petit, je ___ (jouer) dans le jardin.'
questions.explanation: 'Je jouais' (imparfait) = I used to play / was playing. Describes a habitual past action in childhood.
